record.title: Accessible Cayley graph tree-amalgamation conjecture
record.statement: Let $G$ be an accessible Cayley graph. A **tree amalgamation** is the graph operation used in the paper to assemble graphs along a tree of identifying sets, and a subdivision is obtained by subdividing edges. **Accessible Cayley graph tree-amalgamation conjecture.** Every accessible Cayley graph $G$ can be obtained as the tree amalgamation of subdivisions of one or more Cayley graphs, each of which is either finite or 1-ended. This proposed generalization removes the paper's planarity and cubicity restrictions and is presented as a direction suggested by the results.
record.source_name: Agelos Georgakopoulos, “The planar cubic Cayley graphs”, arXiv:1102.2087 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1102.2087

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2011).

record.title: Strang's bandwidth factorization conjecture for permutation matrices
record.statement: Let $P$ be a finite permutation matrix of bandwidth $w>0$, where bandwidth $1$ means tridiagonal. A bandwidth--1 permutation matrix has nonzero entries only on the main diagonal and the two adjacent diagonals. **Strang's conjecture.** $P$ can be written as the product of at most $2w-1$ bandwidth--1 permutation matrices. This conjecture asks for a uniform sharp factorization bound in terms of bandwidth; the supplied source gives no resolution status.

record.title: The non-power word surjectivity conjecture for PSL(2,q)
record.statement:
Let $F_2$ be the free group on two generators, and let $w=w(x,y)\in F_2$. Call $w$ a **power word** if there are $v\in F_2$ and $m\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $w(x,y)=v(x,y)^m$.

**Non-power word surjectivity conjecture.** If $w$ is not a power word, then, for $G=\operatorname{PSL}(2,q)$,

$$
w(G)=G.
$$

This is presented as a variant of Shalev's conjecture and is motivated by the paper's trace-map questions. It remains conjectural in the source; the claim concerns all non-power two-variable words on the family $\operatorname{PSL}(2,q)$.
record.source_name: Tatiana Bandman, Shelly Garion and Fritz Grunewald, “On the Surjectivity of Engel Words on PSL(2,q)”, arXiv:1008.1397 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.1397

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of August 2010).

record.title: The implication from Delta-SOS to Phi-SOS for graphs
record.statement: Let $\mathcal G$ be a graph. Say that $\mathcal G$ is $\Delta$-SOS if every relevant Rayleigh difference $\Delta G\{e,f\}$ has the required sum-of-squares representation, and say that it is $\Phi$-SOS if the corresponding $\Phi$-polynomials have such representations. **Delta-SOS implies Phi-SOS.** If $\mathcal G$ is $\Delta$-SOS, then $\mathcal G$ is $\Phi$-SOS. This implication is proposed to bootstrap the sum-of-squares argument through two-sums of graphs; the source gives no proof or resolution.

record.title: No-common-edge shortest paths conjecture for multitriangulations
record.statement:
Let $T$ and $T'$ be $k$-triangulations of the $n$-gon, and let $G_{n,k}$ be their flip graph. A **$k$-relevant edge** is an edge eligible to occur in a $k$-triangulation.

**No-common-edge shortest paths conjecture.**
1. A shortest path in $G_{n,k}$ between $T$ and $T'$ never flips a common edge of $T$ and $T'$.
2. If $f$ is a $k$-relevant edge of $T$, $e$ is the unique bisector of the two $k$-stars of $T$ containing $f$, and $e$ is an edge of $T'$, then some shortest path from $T$ to $T'$ first flips $f$.

The source says the first assertion is known for ordinary triangulations and presents these statements as open in the multitriangulation setting.
record.source_name: Vincent Pilaud, “Multitriangulations, pseudotriangulations and some problems of realization of polytopes”, arXiv:1009.1605 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.1605

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2010).

record.title: Property of inner tableau translation for the weak order
record.statement:
Let $SYT_n$ denote the set of standard Young tableaux with $n$ cells, and let $]_{weak}$ be Melnikov's weak order on $SYT_n$. For tableaux $S,T$ with the same inner tableau $R$, let $S'$ and $T'$ be obtained by replacing $R$ in $S$ and $T$ by another tableau $R'$ of the same shape.

**Property of inner tableau translation.** If

$$
S\mathrel{<_{weak}}T,
$$

then

$$
S'\mathrel{<_{weak}}T'.
$$

This property is known for the Kazhdan–Lusztig and geometric orders; for the weak order, it would provide a self-contained proof that the order is well defined. The paper proves the conjecture in special cases, while the general statement remains unresolved.
record.source_name: Muge Taskin, “Inner tableau translation property of the weak order and related results”, arXiv:1009.4890 (2011).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.4890

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2010).

record.title: Triviality of higher-order compositions on coordinate-harmonic functions
record.statement: Let $A_k$ denote the space of fields with $k$ components, and let $(\ast)$ denote the family of differential operations and directional derivatives considered in the paper. A function or field $\textit{\texttt{f}}\in A_k$, $0\leq k\leq m$, is **coordinate-harmonic** if all its coordinates are harmonic functions. **Coordinate-harmonic triviality conjecture.** All compositions of the third and higher order in $(\ast)$ acting on coordinate-harmonic function $\textit{\texttt{f}}\in A_k$, $0\leq k\leq m$, are trivial. This extends the stated result in $\mathbb{R}^{3}$ and proposes the corresponding triviality for the general setting considered in the paper.
record.source_name: Ivana Jovovic and Branko Malesevic, “Some enumerations of non-trivial compositions of the differential operations and the directional derivative”, arXiv:1011.0189 (2016).

record.title: Farber's basis pair graph connectivity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid with ground set $E(M)$ and rank $r(M)$. Its **basis pair graph** $G(M)$ has as vertices the ordered triples $(A_1,A_2,A_3)$, where $A_1$ and $A_2$ are disjoint bases of $M$ and $A_3=E(M)-(A_1\cup A_2)$. Two vertices are adjacent when they differ by switching a pair of elements in two different sets.

**Farber's conjecture.** The basis pair graph of any matroid is connected.

This conjecture was posed by M. Farber, who proved it for transversal matroids; the source also notes results for graphic and cographic matroids. It remains open in general.
record.source_name: Joseph E. Bonin, “Sparse paving matroids, basis-exchange properties, and cyclic flats”, arXiv:1011.1010 (2010).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.1010

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2010).

record.title: Hiss–Lübeck–Malle-plus conjecture on the planar embedding of the Brauer tree
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite reductive group whose principal $\ell$-block has cyclic defect, and let $h_0$ be the relevant order of the roots of unity occurring in the block. Let $q^\delta$ act on the relevant torus and write its reduction modulo $\ell$ as an element of the group of $h_0$-th roots of unity. **Hiss–Lübeck–Malle-plus conjecture.** The $\ell$-reduction of $q^\delta$ gives a canonical generator of the group of $h_0$-th roots of unity, and the corresponding order induces the cyclic ordering around the exceptional node of the Brauer tree of the principal $\ell$-block of $G$. This is the proposed completion of the conjecture describing the Brauer tree, determining its planar embedding in cases where that embedding is not explicitly known.
record.source_name: Olivier Dudas, “Coxeter orbits and Brauer trees”, arXiv:1011.5476 (2012).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.5476

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2010).

record.title: Gabow's cyclic basis conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a matroid and let

$$
B_1=\{b_1,\ldots,b_r\},\qquad B_2=\{b'_1,\ldots,b'_r\}
$$

be two bases. **Gabow's conjecture.** There exist permutations $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ such that in the sequence

$$
(b_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,b_{\sigma(r)},b'_{\sigma'(1)},\ldots,b'_{\sigma'(r)}),
$$

every set of $r$ cyclically consecutive elements forms a basis. The conjecture strengthens the two-base case of White's basis sequence exchange problem by requiring a cyclic ordering with all consecutive $r$-element windows independent as bases.
record.source_name: Hannaneh Akrami, Siyue Liu, Roshan Raj and László A. Végh, “Matroids are Equitable”, arXiv:2507.12100 (2025).
record.references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2411.01061](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.01061), [arXiv:2302.01445](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01445), [arXiv:1601.03526](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.03526), [arXiv:1110.1826](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.1826), [arXiv:1011.1010](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.1010).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12100

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2025). “The conjecture remains open even for $k=2$, and even if ${\cal X}=(B_1,B_2)$ and ${\cal Y}=(B_2,B_1)$, i.e., we need to swap two bases.”

record.title: The finitely forcible solution conjecture for graphon constraints
record.statement:
Let $F_1,\dots,F_k$ be finite graphs, let $a_1,\dots,a_k$ be prescribed values, and let $t(F_i,W)$ denote the homomorphism density of $F_i$ in a graphon $W$. **Finitely forcible solution conjecture.** If a finite set of constraints

$$
t(F_i,W)=a_i\qquad (i=1,\dots,k)
$$

is satisfied by some graphon, then it is satisfied by a finitely forcible graphon. This would imply that every extremal graph problem has a finitely forcible solution.

record.title: Automatic regularity of Butson matrices
record.statement:
Let $H_n(l)$ be the set of $n\times n$ Hadamard matrices whose entries are $l$-th roots of unity. A Butson matrix is **regular** when the scalar product of each pair of rows decomposes as a sum of cycles, with the cycles corresponding to the prime divisors of $l$. **Regularity conjecture.** Every Butson matrix is regular.

All known examples of Butson matrices in the source appear to be regular, but the asserted automatic regularity is not established there.

record.title: Zhang's unified conjecture for polarized metrized graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be an irreducible polarized metrized graph of genus $\bar{g}\geq2$, with total length $\ell(\Gamma)$, invariants $a(\Gamma)$ and $\epsilon(\Gamma)$, and let $c(\bar{g})$ be a positive number for each $\bar{g}\geq2$. **Zhang's unified conjecture.** The following two inequalities hold:

$$
\frac{\bar{g}-1}{\bar{g}+1}\bigl(\ell(\Gamma)-4\bar{g}\,a(\Gamma)\bigr)\leq\epsilon(\Gamma)\leq12\bar{g}\,a(\Gamma)-(1+c(\bar{g}))\ell(\Gamma).
$$

Zhang introduced this formulation to reduce and unify his first and second conjectures; the source gives no resolution status.

record.title: Hanner inequality conjecture for Type I semi-norming hypergraph pairs
record.statement:
Let $H=(\alpha,\beta)$ be a non-factorizable semi-norming hypergraph pair of Type I with parameter $s\geq 2$. For the associated space $L_H$, the $|H|$-Hanner inequality is

$$
\|f+g\|_H^{|H|}+\|f-g\|_H^{|H|}\leq (\|f\|_H+\|g\|_H)^{|H|}+\left|\|f\|_H-\|g\|_H\right|^{|H|}.
$$

**Hanner inequality conjecture.** Every $L_H$ space satisfies the $|H|$-Hanner inequality. The inequality is known in the paper for non-factorizable semi-norming hypergraph pairs of Type II and Type I with an even integer parameter, while the stated Type I case with $s\geq2$ remains conjectural.

record.title: Whittle's decomposition conjecture for near-regular matroids
record.statement:
A **near-regular matroid** is a matroid representable over every field except possibly $\operatorname{GF}(2)$. A **signed-graphic matroid** is the matroid represented by a signed graph; $1$-, $2$-, and $3$-sums are the standard matroid sum operations.

**Whittle's decomposition conjecture.** Every near-regular matroid can be obtained from signed-graphic matroids, their duals, and members of some finite set by applying $1$-, $2$-, and $3$-sums.

This is proposed as an analogue of Seymour's decomposition theorem for regular matroids. The paper presents it as an open conjecture and shows that a satisfactory decomposition theory for near-regular matroids faces an obstruction.
record.source_name: Dillon Mayhew, Geoff Whittle and Stefan H. M. van Zwam, “An obstacle to a decomposition theorem for near-regular matroids”, arXiv:0905.3252 (2011).

record.title: The degree-two vertex conjecture for random tournaments
record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph, and let $a$, $s$, and $b$ be three distinct vertices in $V$. The events $\{a\to s\}$ and $\{s\to b\}$ record directed reachability in the random tournament associated with $G$.

**Degree-two vertex conjecture.** If $s$ has degree at most two, then the events $\{a\to s\}$ and $\{s\to b\}$ are independent or negatively correlated.

This extends the corresponding result for trees and the established bound for cycles. The claim concerns the sign of the correlation when the distinguished vertex has degree at most two; no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Sven Erick Alm and Svante Linusson, “A counter-intuitive correlation in a random tournament”, arXiv:0906.0240 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.0240

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2009).

record.title: Normality conjecture for cut polytopes of grid graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a grid graph, and let ${\rm Cut}^\square(G)$ denote its cut polytope. Normality means that the affine semigroup generated by the homogenized cut vectors is saturated.

**The grid-graph conjecture.** The cut polytope ${\rm Cut}^\square(G)$ is normal if $G$ is a grid graph.

The source presents this as another conjecture sufficient, together with the preceding reduction, for addressing the Sturmfels–Sullivant normality conjecture. No proof or resolution is given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Hidefumi Ohsugi, “Normality of cut polytopes of graphs is a minor closed property”, arXiv:0906.5303 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.5303

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2009).

record.title: S. B. Rao's well-quasi-ordering conjecture for degree sequences
record.statement:
Let a **graphic degree sequence** be a multiset of non-negative integers realized as the degree sequence of a simple graph. For a degree sequence $D$, let

$$
\mathcal{R}(D)=\{G\mid D(G)=D\}
$$

be its set of realizations. Define $D\preceq D'$ if there exist $G\in\mathcal{R}(D)$ and $G'\in\mathcal{R}(D')$ such that $G$ is an induced subgraph of $G'$. **Rao's conjecture.** The degree sequences are well-quasi-ordered with respect to the relation $\preceq$. Chudnovsky and Seymour announced a proof of this conjecture, so the claim is no longer open.
record.source_name: Zdenek Dvorak and Bojan Mohar, “Chromatic number and complete graph substructures for degree sequences”, arXiv:0907.1583 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.1583

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2009). “Despite many attempts, the Hadwiger Conjecture remains open, thus its relaxations are of high interest.”
